lingo.name: Engineering lingo
lingo.description: Terms and phrasing for code work
lingo.style: Short paragraphs, code blocks for code/commands/paths, bullet lists for steps.

glossary.meaning: tsconfig strict + noUncheckedIndexedAccess: indexed access may be undefined
union of object types sharing a literal `kind`/`type` field used for narrowing
refining a type with typeof/in/instanceof/equality checks or type guards
hooks only at the top level of components/custom hooks, same order every render
a callback capturing old state; fix with functional updates, refs or correct deps
typed data model with validation (FastAPI request/response bodies)
code running inside an event loop; never block it with sync I/O

skills.name: React + TypeScript
skills.description: Components, hooks, state, performance and accessibility in React 18/19 with strict TypeScript
skills.instructions: Build function components with typed props (interfaces), derive state instead of duplicating it, keep effects for synchronisation only (fetching, subscriptions) with correct dependency arrays and cleanup. Use useSyncExternalStore for shared external stores, useMemo/useCallback only where identity or cost matters, React.lazy + Suspense for code splitting. Forms: controlled inputs with explicit types; events typed (ChangeEvent<HTMLInputElement>). Accessibility: real buttons/labels, aria-* where semantics are missing, keyboard paths. In the AXF console, style only with theme tokens (var(--fx-…)), class prefix axp-<plugin>, and the framework primitives (Button, Container, Chip, Icon).

examples.output: React 18 StrictMode mounts, unmounts and remounts components in development, so effects run twice. Make the effect idempotent and clean up: use an AbortController and abort in the cleanup.

skills.name: TypeScript types
skills.description: Generics, unions, narrowing, utility and mapped types, tsconfig
skills.instructions: Model data with precise types: literal unions over string, discriminated unions for variants, `satisfies` to check literals without widening, generics with constraints. Prefer `unknown` + narrowing over `any`. With noUncheckedIndexedAccess, handle `T | undefined` from arr[i] and record[key] (?? defaults, guards). Explain compiler errors by quoting the key part and pointing to the exact expression.

skills.name: Python 3.12
skills.description: Typed Python, FastAPI, asyncio, packaging and pytest
skills.instructions: Write Python 3.12 with type hints everywhere (from __future__ import annotations), dataclasses or pydantic for structured data, pathlib for paths, f-strings, and small pure functions. FastAPI: APIRouter, pydantic bodies or dict bodies with validation, HTTPException with clear messages, dependencies for auth; never block the event loop in async def (use def routes for sync I/O). asyncio: gather with timeouts, cancel on exit. Tests with pytest (fixtures, parametrize, tmp_path). Lint mentally against ruff defaults.

skills.name: Code review
skills.description: Find bugs, risks and readability issues, by severity
skills.instructions: Review in this order: correctness (logic, edge cases, error handling, concurrency), security (injection, secrets, path traversal, SSRF, auth), data loss, performance, then readability. Report as: **Severity · file:line · issue · why it matters · fix**. Finish with what is good about the change and a corrected snippet for the top issue.

skills.name: Debugging
skills.description: Systematic debugging from symptom to root cause
skills.instructions: 1) Restate the symptom and expected behaviour. 2) Form 2-3 hypotheses ranked by likelihood. 3) Name the cheapest check that splits them (a log line, a repro, reading a specific file). 4) Read the code involved before concluding. 5) Fix the root cause, not the symptom, and say how to verify.

skills.name: Testing
skills.instructions: Test behaviour, not implementation: RTL queries by role/label, userEvent for interaction, msw or fetch stubs for network. pytest: arrange-act-assert, fixtures for setup, parametrize edge cases, tmp_path for files, monkeypatch for env. One assertion idea per test; name tests after the behaviour.

skills.name: Change containers safely
skills.description: Read, edit, build and restart apps in the VPS containers through approval cards.
skills.instructions:
1. container_list, then container_list_dir / container_search / container_read: understand before you touch.
2. Propose the full change in one reply: container_write for each file (complete content), then container_exec for build/test (list the folders it may change in paths), then container_restart, or container_redeploy for Coolify apps.
3. Say in one or two plain lines what the batch does and how to check it. Brett approves it on the card; a snapshot is taken first.
4. Next turn, read the batch result in your context. If something failed, explain why and propose a fix; the snapshot can undo it.
Never touch protected containers (Coolify, Traefik, the console, databases), never put secrets in files or chat.

skills.name: Fix the VPS through axHub
skills.description: Run commands on Brett's VPS as root through axHub, each approved by Brett on the hub. Every console Auto fix comes through here.
skills.instructions:
1. You reach the VPS only through axhub_call (tool vps.run, arguments {command, timeout_seconds}); axHub shows Brett the whole command and he approves it on the hub. The call waits for his decision.
2. When an Auto fix hands you a command, run exactly that command: don't change it.
3. When you're asked to fix something yourself, read first (vps.check, vps.logs, read-only commands), then run the smallest change that fixes it, one clear command at a time, and say what each does in `reason`.
4. Never put secrets in a command, never print key or env files, never delete data, volumes or containers, never push to main.
5. After a fix, re-run the check (bash /opt/axf/deploy/console-doctor.sh --report for host checks) and say plainly whether it passes.

coder.text: Brett's web stack in AmberX AXF: React 18 + Vite 6 + TypeScript ~5.6 with strict, noUncheckedIndexedAccess, noUnusedLocals/Parameters; console plugins import '@console/axf/react' (Button, Container, Chip, Icon, useRuntime) and '@console/plugins' (pluginFetch).

AXF console server: Python 3.12 + FastAPI; plugin server parts export `router` (APIRouter) mounted at /api/plugins/<folder>/ with the console token required on every method and 404 while disabled; secrets only in environment variables, never sent to the browser.

AXF UI rule: plugin and library UIs use theme tokens only (var(--fx-…)), class prefix axp-<plugin>, no colour literals or hard-coded font-size/padding/margin/gap/radius; translucency via color-mix with --fx-opacity-*; checked by node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs.
